ai.description: The Gundia frog (30–40 mm) is brown with dark dorsal mottling and a distinct pale snout tip. It features prominent dorsolateral folds and long, slender limbs adapted for leaping in rocky streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana gundia* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, narrow white or pale vertebral stripe running along the center of its back, which is absent in similar congeners.
ai.habitat: *Indirana gundia* inhabits the leaf litter of primary evergreen tropical rainforests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Gundia frog is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by leaping into fast-flowing streams to escape predators when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana gundia* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 100–200 eggs in moist rock crevices or mossy areas where larvae develop semi-terrestrially.
ai.distributionRemarks: Indirana gundia is endemic to the central Western Ghats in Karnataka, India, specifically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests within the Gundia River basin.
ai.callDescription: The Gundia Frog produces a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps that are heard near fast-flowing streams in the Western Ghats.
